'''Thomas S. K. Chang''' (1948-1996) was an American [[reproductive medicine|reproductive biologist]]. He was born in Hawaii in 1948, and earned a bachelor's degree and Ph.D. from the [[University of Hawaiʻi]] in 1970 and 1976.<ref name="In Memoriam">{{cite journal | title=IN MEMORIAM Dr. Thomas S.K. Chang, 1948-1996 |author=Donald S. Coffey |author2=Barry R Zirkin | journal=[[Biology of Reproduction]]  | volume=55 | issue=3| year=1996 | pages= 729 |doi = 10.1093/biolreprod/55.3.729 | doi-access=free}}</ref> In 1977, he came to The [[Johns Hopkins School of Hygiene and Public Health]] to carry out his postdoctoral studies. In 1981, he joined the Department of Urology of The [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]] to carry out his postdoctoral studies.<ref>{{cite journal | author= Zirkin BR | title= Involvement of an acrosinlike proteinase in the sulfhydryl-induced degradation of rabbit sperm nuclear protamine | author2= Chang TS | author3= Heaps J | journal=[[J Cell Biol]] | volume=85 | issue=1| year=1980 | pages= 116–121 |pmid = 6988441 | pmc= 2110599 | doi= 10.1083/jcb.85.1.116 }}</ref> His studies focus on [[male infertility]] in relationship to [[sperm]] physiology and [[endocrinology]].<ref>{{cite journal | title=Sperm nuclear packing and regulation during spermatogenesis and fertilization | author= Zirkin BR | author2= Soucek DA | author3= Chang TS | journal=[[Johns Hopkins Med J]] | volume=151 | issue=3| year=1982 | pages= 101–112 |pmid = 6810011}}</ref>

The Thomas S. K. Chang Merit Award, established in 1996, is awarded annually by the American Society of Andrology.<ref>[https://andrologysociety.org/awards/trainee-awards/thomas-s-k-chang-merit-award.aspx Thomas S. K. Chang Merit Award], American Society of Andrology. Accessed 2019-08-30.</ref>
